targetText: at a certain stage of its development concentration itself, as it were, leads straight to monopoly
summary: Free competition naturally destroys itself over time. As successful companies grow into giants, it becomes easier for a few huge firms to agree among themselves to control prices and divide markets, creating monopolies.
context: Lenin refutes early 20th-century economists who believed free competition was permanent. He shows how competitive markets naturally evolve into corporate oligopolies and cartels as production becomes concentrated in fewer hands.

targetText: This transformation of competition into monopoly is one of the most important
summary: The shift from open competition between thousands of small business owners to dominance by a small group of massive corporations is the defining transition into monopoly capitalism.
context: By the early 1900s, key industries (steel, oil, mining, electricity) had transitioned from competitive local markets into cartelized industries controlled by corporate boards, reshaping the entire global economy.

targetText: Production becomes social, but appropriation remains private.
summary: Modern production relies on global supply chains and millions of coordinated workers (socialized production), but the profits and ownership remain locked in the hands of a small group of private investors (private appropriation).
context: This is a core structural contradiction of capitalism: society functions as an interconnected web of collective labor, but private capitalists retain exclusive ownership and decision-making power over the resulting wealth.
